Handoff from a PR-triage session. Four open PRs in entireio/cli, all by the external contributor `stale2000`, all filed 2026-06-09/10, all still open. Please investigate each one and give me a per-PR verdict: is the bug real on current origin/main, is the fix correct, and what should happen to the PR.

My triage already established the following against origin/main. Treat it as a starting point to verify, not as ground truth - I want you to check each claim yourself and tell me where I'm wrong.

## #1396 [bug] Restore native Windows interactive prompts
Files: cmd/entire/cli/interactive/{interactive.go,tty*.go}, login.go, strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go
What I found: `CanPromptInteractively()` (cmd/entire/cli/interactive/interactive.go, the /dev/tty open near line 55) has no `runtime.GOOS` branch anywhere. On Windows the `os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", ...)` fails, the function returns false, and every interactive prompt in the CLI is silently suppressed. `interactive/rawmode_other.go` states the assumption out loud: "Those platforms don't have a /dev/tty for CanPromptInteractively to open either, so this path is not reached in practice." I grepped for `GOOS == "windows"` across non-test, non-md files and found it only in agent/registry.go, testutil/testutil.go, e2e/agents/claude.go and internal/entireclient/userdirs/userdirs.go - none of them terminal detection. WINDOWS.md only records that interactive *tests* are skipped on Windows (line 70), which is consistent with nobody having noticed the product gap.
This PR has ZERO reviews. Highest priority of the four.
Worth determining: what does a Windows user actually lose today (which prompts), and does the PR's tty_windows.go approach match how the repo handles other platform splits.

## #1394 [bug] Preserve Claude subagent token totals during condensation
Files: cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go
What I found: main still passes `""` as the subagents dir at BOTH call sites - manual_commit_condensation.go:1471 and :1517 (`agent.CalculateTokenUsage(ctx, ag, data.Transcript, checkpointTranscriptStart, "")`). Those are exactly the two lines the PR changes. Notably the `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` marker that used to sit on those lines has since been DELETED from main without the behaviour changing, so the signpost is gone but the bug isn't.
The PR author himself flagged uncertainty in the description ("I noticed the log saying that the bug might be intentional? Or it is unknown why it is written this way?"). Please settle that question: is passing "" deliberate, and if so where is that recorded? Check whether the subagents dir path the PR constructs (`filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(transcriptPath), sessionID, "subagents")`) is right for each agent, not just Claude Code.

## #1408 [bug] Fix rewind of tracked checkpoint deletions
Files: cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go, rewind_test.go
What I found: neither `deleteTrackedFilesMissingFromCheckpoint` nor `trackedFilesInTree` exists on main, and main's `Rewind` still only deletes *untracked* files absent from the checkpoint - it ignores tracked files that the checkpoint doesn't contain. ZERO reviews.
The author wrote "I'm having a difficult time wrapping my head around this bug, but the logs pretty clearly keep insisting that there is an issue." So the diagnosis needs independent confirmation. Build the scenario and prove or disprove it: does `entire checkpoint rewind` leave behind a tracked file that the checkpoint says was deleted? Note the PR also swallows a context-cancellation error that main currently ignores via `//nolint:errcheck`, so check the error handling change on its own merits.

## #1391 [cleanup] Centralize form accessibility behavior
Files: strategy/manual_commit_reset.go, strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go, uiform/uiform_test.go, versioncheck/autoupdate.go
What I found: this one appears to have ALREADY LANDED by other means. `isAccessibleMode` and `WithAccessible` are gone from cmd/entire/cli/strategy/, and `huh.NewForm` is now called in exactly one non-test place: cmd/entire/cli/uiform/uiform.go:83. That is what the PR proposed. So I expect the verdict here is "close as already done" - please confirm, and check whether the PR's source-level guard test (the thing that keeps `huh.NewForm` centralized) exists on main in any form. If it doesn't, that guard is the one piece worth salvaging.
Side finding while I was there: CLAUDE.md lines ~1570-1591 still document the OLD pattern - it tells contributors to call `NewAccessibleForm()` instead of `huh.NewForm()`, and describes an `isAccessibleMode()` helper in the strategy package. Both are stale now. Since CLAUDE.md is the instruction file agents read, that section is actively pointing people at code that no longer exists. Please confirm and note it; it needs its own small fix.

## Constraints
- Do NOT post anything to GitHub - no PR comments, no reviews, no issue creation. Report back to me and I'll handle the posting.
- Do NOT push to any branch.
- Do NOT use `git stash` / `git stash pop` - the stash stack is shared across all worktrees on this machine and other sessions may be using it. Use a temporary WIP commit if you need to set work aside.
- Work only in your own worktree (/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/soph-bugfixes-issues). Don't cd into other worktrees or the main checkout.
- Fetch the PR heads read-only if you need the diffs: `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr<N>`.

## What I want back
For each of the four: (1) is the bug real on current main - yes/no, with file:line evidence; (2) is the PR's fix correct and complete, or does it need changes; (3) recommendation - merge as-is / needs rebase / needs rework / close as already fixed; (4) for anything you close or reject, the reference a human can cite.
Three of these four have never had a human look at them in three months, and the author is an outside contributor, so accuracy matters more than speed here.

+package interactive
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+)
+
+// PromptTTY is a platform prompt terminal opened for both input and output.
+type PromptTTY struct {
+	in  *os.File
+	out *os.File
+}
+
+// Read reads prompt input.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := t.in.Read(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, fmt.Errorf("read prompt terminal: %w", err)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// Write writes prompt output.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := t.out.Write(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, fmt.Errorf("write prompt terminal: %w", err)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// Close closes the prompt terminal handles.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Close() error {
+	err := t.in.Close()
+	if t.out != t.in {
+		if outErr := t.out.Close(); err == nil {
+			err = outErr
+		}
+	}
+	return err
+}

+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+)
+
+// OpenPromptTTY opens the Windows console devices for interactive prompts.
+func OpenPromptTTY() (*PromptTTY, error) {
+	in, err := os.OpenFile("CONIN$", os.O_RDONLY, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("open CONIN$: %w", err)
+	}
+	out, err := os.OpenFile("CONOUT$", os.O_WRONLY, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		_ = in.Close()
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("open CONOUT$: %w", err)
+	}
+	return &PromptTTY{in: in, out: out}, nil
+}

1	// Package interactive provides TTY-related helpers shared between the cli
     2	// and strategy packages without inducing an import cycle (strategy cannot
     3	// import cli).
     4	package interactive
     5	
     6	import (
     7		"io"
     8		"os"
     9		"testing"
    10	
    11		"golang.org/x/term"
    12	)
    13	
    14	// EnvTestTTY is the env-var name for the force-interactive test override.
    15	//   - EnvTestTTY=1 → CanPromptInteractively returns true.
    16	//   - EnvTestTTY set to any other value → returns false.
    17	//   - EnvTestTTY unset → real detection via testing.Testing(), agent
    18	//     sentinels, CI, then /dev/tty probe.
    19	const EnvTestTTY = "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY"
    20	
    21	// CanPromptInteractively reports whether interactive confirmation prompts
    22	// (huh forms, yes/no questions, etc.) can be shown. Returns false in CI,
    23	// agent subprocesses that inherit a TTY but can't respond to prompts,
    24	// and other environments without a controlling TTY.
    25	//
    26	// Precedence (first match wins):
    27	//  1. EnvTestTTY=1 forces interactive ON; any other non-empty value forces OFF.
    28	//  2. testing.Testing() — `go test` runs default to OFF so in-process tests
    29	//     don't hang on developer terminals that happen to have a real /dev/tty.
    30	//     Subprocess tests must spawn via execx.NonInteractive (or set EnvTestTTY).
    31	//  3. Agent sentinels — vendor-set by agent subprocesses.
    32	//  4. CI=<non-empty-non-false> — de-facto CI convention.
    33	//  5. /dev/tty probe, plus its terminal mode: a controlling terminal held in
    34	//     raw mode belongs to a full-screen TUI (lazygit, gitui, tig, …) that
    35	//     spawned us, not to a shell we can prompt. See rawmode_unix.go.
    36	func CanPromptInteractively() bool {
    37		if v := os.Getenv(EnvTestTTY); v != "" {
    38			return v == "1"
    39		}
    40		if testing.Testing() {
    41			return false
    42		}
    43		if isAgentSubprocessEnv() {
    44			return false
    45		}
    46		// CI=<non-empty> is the de-facto CI-provider convention (GitHub Actions,
    47		// CircleCI, GitLab, Travis, Buildkite). Self-hosted runners expose /dev/tty,
    48		// so the probe below isn't enough — an interactive prompt on CI hangs.
    49		// CI=false is the `is-ci` escape hatch for developers who need to override
    50		// an inherited value.
    51		if v := os.Getenv("CI"); v != "" && v != "false" {
    52			return false
    53		}
    54	
    55		tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    56		if err != nil {
    57			return false
    58		}
    59		defer tty.Close()
    60		// Having a controlling terminal isn't enough — a TUI that spawned us holds
    61		// that same terminal in raw mode for its own screen and keys. See
    62		// rawmode_unix.go.
    63		return !ttyInRawMode(tty)
    64	}
    65	
    66	// UnderTest reports whether the process is running in a test context — either
    67	// inside `go test` (testing.Testing()) or with EnvTestTTY explicitly set. Use
    68	// to skip operations that read from the real terminal (e.g. opening /dev/tty)
    69	// even when CanPromptInteractively() returns true.
    70	func UnderTest() bool {
    71		return testing.Testing() || os.Getenv(EnvTestTTY) != ""
    72	}
    73	
    74	// agentSubprocessEnvVars are vendor-set variables that mark a process spawned
    75	// by an agent's shell tool or hook runner. Presence alone is the signal —
    76	// vendors spell the value differently ("1", "true"), so only an empty or unset
    77	// value means absent.
    78	//
    79	// This is the single source of truth for the list: isAgentSubprocessEnv reads
    80	// it, and the tests both enumerate it and clear it. Adding a name here is the
    81	// whole change.
    82	//
    83	//   - CLAUDECODE is deliberately absent. Claude Code sets it to 1 in its tool
    84	//     subprocesses, so it could join this list, but doing so withdraws every
    85	//     interactive prompt from the largest agent population at once. That is a
    86	//     product call, not a detection fix.
    87	var agentSubprocessEnvVars = []string{
    88		"COPILOT_CLI",     // Copilot CLI hook subprocesses (v0.0.421+)
    89		"CURSOR_AGENT",    // cursor-agent shell tool; set alongside CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID
    90		"GEMINI_CLI",      // Gemini CLI shell tool (https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/shell/)
    91		"OPENCODE",        // set on opencode's own process, so every child inherits it
    92		"PI_CODING_AGENT", // Pi Coding Agent shell tool
    93	}
    94	
    95	// isAgentSubprocessEnv reports whether the env indicates we're running inside
    96	// an agent subprocess that inherited a TTY but can't respond to prompts:
    97	// either one of agentSubprocessEnvVars is set, or GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 —
    98	// the caller (CI, Factory AI Droid, etc.) asked git to stop prompting, and we
    99	// respect it from git-hook context too.
   100	//
   101	// GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT stays outside the list because its semantics differ: it
   102	// is a tri-state the user may legitimately set to "1", so only the exact value
   103	// "0" counts, where the others are presence checks.
   104	func isAgentSubprocessEnv() bool {
   105		for _, name := range agentSubprocessEnvVars {
   106			if os.Getenv(name) != "" {
   107				return true
   108			}
   109		}
   110		return os.Getenv("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT") == "0"

     1	//go:build darwin || linux
     2	
     3	package interactive
     4	
     5	import (
     6		"os"
     7	
     8		"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
     9	)
    10	
    11	// ttyInRawMode reports whether the terminal behind f has canonical (line) input
    12	// disabled — i.e. a full-screen program owns the screen rather than a shell we
    13	// can prompt.
    14	//
    15	// Terminal-UI git clients (lazygit, gitui, tig, …) run git as a child process
    16	// while keeping the controlling terminal in raw mode for their own screen and
    17	// key handling. Such a child — including a git hook, and therefore `entire` —
    18	// still inherits that controlling terminal, so it can open /dev/tty
    19	// successfully. The /dev/tty probe alone therefore cannot tell a TUI apart from
    20	// a shell, and prompting there is broken in both directions: our output paints
    21	// over the TUI's screen, and our line read races the TUI's key reader for the
    22	// user's keystrokes, so the answer may never arrive and the git command appears
    23	// to hang (the reported symptom was lazygit freezing on the "Link this commit
    24	// to session context?" prompt).
    25	//
    26	// Canonical input mode (ICANON) is the signal that separates the two: a shell
    27	// restores the terminal to canonical mode before running a foreground command,
    28	// while a TUI holds it in raw mode for as long as it owns the screen. That is
    29	// also exactly the distinction the TUIs themselves draw — lazygit restores
    30	// cooked mode when it deliberately hands the terminal to a child (editor,
    31	// interactive rebase, custom subprocess commands), which is when prompting does
    32	// work and should happen.
    33	//
    34	// Checking the terminal mode rather than the hook's file descriptors is
    35	// deliberate: git's hook stdio plumbing varies by git version (stdin is
    36	// /dev/null, and stdout/stderr may be inherited or captured), so an isatty
    37	// check on those descriptors is not a stable signal, while terminal ownership
    38	// is.
    39	//
    40	// rawModeIoctl is the platform's termios read ioctl (rawmode_darwin.go,
    41	// rawmode_linux.go); rawmode_other.go covers platforms without termios.
    42	func ttyInRawMode(f *os.File) bool {
    43		termios, err := unix.IoctlGetTermios(int(f.Fd()), rawModeIoctl) //nolint:gosec // G115: uintptr->int is safe for fd
    44		if err != nil {
    45			// Can't tell — fail open so an unexpected ioctl failure never silently
    46			// disables prompting. This check may only ever suppress prompts we
    47			// positively know are unusable.
    48			return false
    49		}
    50		return termios.Lflag&unix.ICANON == 0
    51	}

1	// Package uiform builds huh forms wired to Entire's standard theme and
     2	// accessibility behavior. Centralises the Theme()+WithAccessible() recipe
     3	// so picker UI stays consistent across callers.
     4	package uiform
     5	
     6	import (
     7		"context"
     8		"errors"
     9		"fmt"
    10		"os"
    11	
    12		"charm.land/huh/v2"
    13		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
    14	
    15		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/palette"
    16	)
    17	
    18	// IsAccessibleMode reports whether accessibility mode is enabled via the
    19	// ACCESSIBLE environment variable. Set ACCESSIBLE=1 (or any non-empty
    20	// value) to enable simpler prompts that work better with screen readers.
    21	func IsAccessibleMode() bool {
    22		return os.Getenv("ACCESSIBLE") != ""
    23	}
    24	
    25	// Theme returns Entire's standard huh theme: base16 (ANSI 0–15) colors so
    26	// form prompts respect the user's terminal palette and stay consistent with
    27	// the rest of the CLI's styling. Derived from huh.ThemeBase16 with a few
    28	// overrides — magenta selection (pointer + chosen options); titles and
    29	// unselected options use the terminal's default foreground so they invert
    30	// with the background (dark text on light, light text on dark) like the
    31	// checkbox bracket does.
    32	func Theme() huh.Theme {
    33		return huh.ThemeFunc(func(isDark bool) *huh.Styles {
    34			t := huh.ThemeBase16(isDark)
    35	
    36			accent := lipgloss.Color(palette.Accent)
    37			lightDark := lipgloss.LightDark(isDark)
    38	
    39			// Titles and unselected options drop their explicit color and inherit
    40			// the terminal's default text color, which already inverts with the
    41			// background. A pinned base16 slot (e.g. black "0") can't invert because
    42			// it always maps to that slot in both themes. Group.Title is copied from
    43			// Focused.Title inside ThemeBase16, and ThemeBase16 copies Focused into
    44			// Blurred wholesale, so clear the blurred variants too — otherwise
    45			// inactive fields in multi-field forms keep the pinned base16 color.
    46			t.Focused.Title = t.Focused.Title.UnsetForeground()
    47			t.Group.Title = t.Group.Title.UnsetForeground()
    48			t.Focused.UnselectedOption = t.Focused.UnselectedOption.UnsetForeground()
    49			t.Blurred.Title = t.Blurred.Title.UnsetForeground()
    50			t.Blurred.UnselectedOption = t.Blurred.UnselectedOption.UnsetForeground()
    51	
    52			// Magenta selection: the pointer (single + multi select) and the
    53			// chosen option(s), replacing ThemeBase16's yellow/green.
    54			t.Focused.SelectSelector = t.Focused.SelectSelector.Foreground(accent)
    55			t.Focused.MultiSelectSelector = t.Focused.MultiSelectSelector.Foreground(accent)
    56			t.Focused.SelectedOption = t.Focused.SelectedOption.Foreground(accent)
    57			t.Focused.SelectedPrefix = t.Focused.SelectedPrefix.Foreground(accent)
    58	
    59			// Blurred (inactive) button: no background chip and default text color,
    60			// so it reads as plain text that inverts with the terminal theme while
    61			// the focused button keeps its magenta/accent chip. Set both the focused
    62			// and blurred field variants (ThemeBase16 copies Focused into Blurred).
    63			t.Focused.BlurredButton = t.Focused.BlurredButton.UnsetForeground().UnsetBackground()
    64			t.Blurred.BlurredButton = t.Blurred.BlurredButton.UnsetForeground().UnsetBackground()
    65	
    66			// Focused (selected) button: keep the magenta chip, but use the inverse
    67			// of the default foreground — i.e. the terminal's background color — so
    68			// the label reads as reverse video against the chip (light on light

    78	// New creates a huh form with the standard theme, switching to accessible
    79	// mode when ACCESSIBLE is set. WithAccessible is only available on forms
    80	// (not individual fields), so wrap confirmations and other prompts in a
    81	// form to opt into accessibility.
    82	func New(groups ...*huh.Group) *huh.Form {
    83		form := huh.NewForm(groups...).WithTheme(Theme())
    84		if IsAccessibleMode() {
    85			form = form.WithAccessible(true)
    86		}
    87		return form
    88	}

    90	// SingleLineMultiSelectHeight reserves three rows for rendered field headers.
    91	// Callers with multiline options or headers taller than three rows need a
    92	// different height strategy. The form still clamps this on short terminals.
    93	func SingleLineMultiSelectHeight(optionCount int) int {
    94		const headerRows = 3
    95		return optionCount + headerRows
    96	}
    97	
    98	// PromptYN renders a Confirm form with the standard theme/accessibility
    99	// behavior and returns the user's answer. On user cancellation (Ctrl+C or
   100	// context.Canceled) returns (false, nil) so callers treat it as a "no";
   101	// on real form errors the error is returned wrapped.
   102	func PromptYN(ctx context.Context, question string, def bool) (bool, error) {
   103		answer := def
   104		form := New(huh.NewGroup(
   105			huh.NewConfirm().
   106				Title(question).
   107				Value(&answer),
   108		))
   109		if err := form.RunWithContext(ctx); err != nil {
   110			if errors.Is(err, huh.ErrUserAborted) || errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
   111				return false, nil
   112			}
   113			return false, fmt.Errorf("confirm form: %w", err)
   114		}
   115		return answer, nil
   116	}

Remove the restore half of the rewind machinery
The `rewind` commands were removed a while ago and nothing replaced them,
so the code that puts files back on disk from a checkpoint has had no
caller outside its own tests ever since. A whole-program VTA call graph
rooted at every cobra command constructor, every package initializer and
every main confirms it: Rewind, PreviewRewind, CanRewind and
checkCanRewindWithWarning each come back with zero reachable owners, while
GetRewindPoints, GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints and ResolveAgentForRewind next to
them still have real ones. CLAUDE.md has been calling this "machinery
pending removal" in so many words; this is the removal.

Gone from manual_commit_rewind.go: Rewind (the worktree overwrite),
resetShadowBranchToCheckpoint (only Rewind called it), CanRewind, and
PreviewRewind. Gone from strategy.go: RewindPreview, which only
PreviewRewind constructed. Gone from common.go: checkCanRewindWithWarning,
whose only caller was CanRewind, and with it countLines and
computeDiffStats, which nothing else in the package called. The last two
are in the same commit rather than a follow-up because leaving them behind
for one commit fails the `unused` linter, and a commit that does not pass
lint is worse than a slightly wider one. splitLines stays -- content_overlap.go
uses it. The countLines in cmd/entire/cli/explain.go is a separate function
and is untouched.

Deliberately kept, because they are live: GetRewindPoints and
GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints feed `entire checkpoint list --pending`;
RestoreLogsOnly and everything under it (restoredPromptPreview,
FirstDisplayPrompt, extractPromptsFromTranscriptBytes,
ResolveAgentForRewind, readSessionPrompt, classifySessionsForRestore,
ClassifyTimestamps, ResolveLatestCheckpointFromMap) feed `entire resume`
and `entire trail resume`. RestoreLogsOnly writes session logs, not
worktree files, so it is not part of what went. The RewindPoint,
RestoredSession and SessionRestoreStatus types and the "rewind point"
vocabulary are unchanged.

Tests for the removed behaviour go with it: the two PreviewRewind tests,
the three CanRewind tests, and the three Rewind execution tests including
TestShadowStrategy_Rewind_PreservesIgnoredFiles, which guarded the restore
path against reaching for go-git's Worktree.Reset. That hazard cannot be
hit by code that no longer exists; the go-git rule itself still stands in
CLAUDE.md for the paths that do checkout and reset.

refactor(checkpoint): use the existing token-summing primitive, and cap its depth
Review of the previous commit found the store-side half was reinventing
types.AddTokenUsage, which already sums the five scalars and recurses into
SubagentTokens, is already imported by persistent.go, and is already used in
production by agentimport. Two reviewers verified equivalence independently, one
by probing both against 7 shapes. Shipping as written would have taken the repo
from three hand-rolled TokenUsage adders to four, with the newest one being the
one whose own comment explained that a field-by-field copy is how the nested
total came to be dropped. aggregateTokenUsage, subagentTokensOf and their new
test are gone; the single caller now calls types.AddTokenUsage.

Propagating the nested total into the root summary turned out to introduce a
write-amplification vector, which the drop had been masking: token usage is read
back from per-session metadata.json blobs on the shared checkpoint branch, so the
chain depth is not trustworthy, and the root summary is re-marshalled with
indentation — O(depth²) in output size. A ~10k-deep chain (json's own nesting
limit) in a 200KB session blob measured out to a ~700MB root blob, written and
pushed. AddTokenUsage now truncates at MaxSubagentDepth = 16, matching the
existing reviewTokenMaxDepth convention. Real chains are depth 1.

Condensation side:

- The fill is now the else-branch of the whole-value fallback above it rather
  than a third sequential assignment. The two are mutually exclusive:
  accumulateTokenUsage already carries SubagentTokens, so the fill's guard always
  early-returned when that branch fired — it was dead work.
- Renamed to withSubagentTokensFrom and used for the identical copy-fill block
  inside applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage (9 lines to 1). The abstraction was
  built and then not applied to the existing caller, leaving the load-bearing
  copy-not-mutate invariant documented in two places that could drift.
- Guards collapsed to one condition; doc comment cut from 26 lines to 15 by
  dropping bug history and a paragraph duplicated at the recompute site.

The live-path comment claimed subagentsDir="" for "the same reason" as the
shadow path. That was inverted: mid-turn the subagent transcripts are still on
disk, so the cleanup hazard cannot apply there — it is the one place the
documented gap could actually be closed. Both comments now say what is true, and
carry the measured ~29x cost that justifies the choice on both paths.

Tests: the new condensation tests folded into the file that already owns subagent
token invariants (renamed subagent_token_dedup_test.go -> subagent_tokens_test.go);
the second one was ~50 lines of arrangement duplicated from the existing
real-reset-path test wrapped around 6 unique assertions, so those assertions now
extend that test instead. The hand-rolled metadata-branch walker is replaced by
the store's own Read, which does not hard-code the sharded layout. A reviewer
disproved the copy-semantics assertions empirically — they pass against a
mutate-in-place implementation, because applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage already
returns a copy on that path — so they are replaced by a direct unit test on the
pure function.

+package interactive
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+)
+
+// PromptTTY is a platform prompt terminal opened for both input and output.
+type PromptTTY struct {
+	in  *os.File
+	out *os.File
+}
+
+// Read reads prompt input.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := t.in.Read(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, fmt.Errorf("read prompt terminal: %w", err)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// Write writes prompt output.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := t.out.Write(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, fmt.Errorf("write prompt terminal: %w", err)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// Close closes the prompt terminal handles.
+func (t *PromptTTY) Close() error {
+	err := t.in.Close()
+	if t.out != t.in {
+		if outErr := t.out.Close(); err == nil {
+			err = outErr
+		}
+	}
+	return err
+}

+//go:build windows
+
+package interactive
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+)
+
+// OpenPromptTTY opens the Windows console devices for interactive prompts.
+func OpenPromptTTY() (*PromptTTY, error) {
+	in, err := os.OpenFile("CONIN$", os.O_RDONLY, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("open CONIN$: %w", err)
+	}
+	out, err := os.OpenFile("CONOUT$", os.O_WRONLY, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		_ = in.Close()
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("open CONOUT$: %w", err)
+	}
+	return &PromptTTY{in: in, out: out}, nil
+}

   512	}
   513	
   514	func remapRewriteSHA(sha string, rewrites []rewritePair) (string, bool) {
   515		for _, pair := range rewrites {
   516			if sha == pair.OldSHA {
   517				return pair.NewSHA, true
   518			}
   519		}
   520		return sha, false
   521	}

   523	func shadowBranchExistsForBaseCommit(repo *git.Repository, baseCommit, worktreeID string) bool {
   524		if repo == nil || baseCommit == "" {
   525			return false
   526		}
   527	
   528		refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, worktreeID))
   529		_, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   530		return err == nil
   531	}

   533	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) remapSessionForRewrite(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState, rewrites []rewritePair) (bool, error) {
   534		if state == nil {
   535			return false, nil
   536		}
   537	
   538		newBaseCommit, baseChanged := remapRewriteSHA(state.BaseCommit, rewrites)
   539		newAttrBaseCommit, attrChanged := remapRewriteSHA(state.AttributionBaseCommit, rewrites)
   540		if !baseChanged && !attrChanged {
   541			return false, nil
   542		}
   543	
   544		hadShadowBranch := shadowBranchExistsForBaseCommit(repo, state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   545		if baseChanged {
   546			changed, err := s.migrateShadowBranchToBaseCommit(ctx, repo, state, newBaseCommit)
   547			if err != nil {
   548				return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to migrate rewritten shadow branch: %w", err)
   549			}
   550			baseChanged = changed
   551		}
   552	
   553		// If a shadow branch existed, preserve AttributionBaseCommit so future
   554		// attribution still diffs against the original checkpoint base captured on
   555		// that branch. Without a shadow branch, keep attribution in sync with the
   556		// rewritten commit lineage.
   557		if attrChanged && !hadShadowBranch {
   558			state.AttributionBaseCommit = newAttrBaseCommit
   559		}
   560	
   561		return baseChanged || attrChanged, nil
   562	}

   566		allStates, err := s.listAllSessionStates(ctx)

   569		}

   572		for _, state := range allStates {

   574				matching = append(matching, state)
   575			}
   576		}

74e9f831070f19325bb88a7d994c3f3a814cbfe8 | 2026-08-30 | Remove the restore half of the rewind machinery
Committed checkpoints reported "subagent_tokens": null even for sessions that
ran many subagents — 0 of 30 sampled real checkpoints carried one. Two
independent drops:

1. Condensation recomputes token usage from the transcript with
   subagentsDir="", which by contract leaves SubagentTokens nil, and that
   recomputed value replaced what SaveStep had produced. The session-wide
   cumulative survived on state.TokenUsage (so `entire status` still showed
   subagent usage), but the value written to checkpoint metadata lost it.

2. The store's aggregateTokenUsage, which sums a checkpoint's sessions into the
   root metadata.json, copied only the five scalar fields — so even a
   per-session metadata carrying SubagentTokens produced a null total at the
   root.

For (1), fill from state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens: SaveStep already
rescoped it to this window (cumulative minus SubagentTokensBaseline), so
checkpoints stay summable instead of each re-reporting the session total, and
we avoid re-reading subagent transcripts that may already be cleaned up. The
fill copies rather than mutates — state.TokenUsage can alias that struct after
applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage adopts it (Copilot CLI), and mutating would
overwrite the cumulative with a window delta, making resetCheckpointWindow
snapshot a too-small baseline. It also runs after that helper, which must see
the recomputed usage without the fill.

For (2), recurse into SubagentTokens. Summing is correct at that level: it
aggregates across the sessions of one checkpoint, and each session's value is
already checkpoint-scoped. (The replace-don't-add rule applies to accumulating
steps within a session, where each step re-reports a cumulative snapshot.)

Replaces the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` markers with
the actual reason. Known gap, now documented: a mid-turn commit that condenses
before any SaveStep in the window has no CheckpointTokenUsage to draw on and
still records no subagent tokens.

## #1396 — Restore native Windows interactive prompts

### 1. Bug real on current main? **Yes**

`CanPromptInteractively` still unconditionally opens `/dev/tty`:

- `cmd/entire/cli/interactive/interactive.go:55`
- `cmd/entire/cli/interactive/rawmode_other.go:7-10` explicitly acknowledges Windows cannot reach the path.

Additional direct `/dev/tty` dependencies remain:

- Login key availability: `cmd/entire/cli/login.go:99`
- Login key reader: `cmd/entire/cli/login.go:872`
- Commit-link confirmation: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:77`

Consequently, native Windows always takes the non-interactive branch unless `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1` is forced. Depending on the command, Windows users lose or bypass:

- Browser-first login and login URL key actions
- Session/resume and placement pickers
- Confirmation forms, including destructive-operation confirmation
- Interactive runner setup
- Commit-link confirmation—the hook auto-links instead at `manual_commit_hooks.go:485-487`
- Other gated doctor, trail, plugin, repo, setup, review, and investigation flows

### 2. PR fix correct and complete? **Correct direction, incomplete for current main**

Using `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` is the appropriate native-console approach, and the platform split is consistent with the repository’s existing OS-specific files. I verified the PR branch compiles both natively and with `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64`.

However, it cannot be merged as currently written:

- It predates the raw-terminal protection added in `508c438e3` and changes `CanPromptInteractively` to return true merely after opening the terminal. A current fix must preserve `ttyInRawMode` on Unix.
- Login has since been substantially rewritten. The PR modifies the removed `waitForEnter` flow and does not fix the two current login `/dev/tty` call sites.
- Its `PromptTTY` abstraction does not directly fit the current login path, which passes an `*os.File` to Bubble Tea and `interactive.IsTerminalReader`.
- It has no runtime-focused Windows tests.

### 3. Recommendation: **Needs rework and rebase**

This is still a high-priority product bug, but not a merge-as-is or rebase-only change. Rework should centralize native console opening, preserve Unix raw-mode suppression, migrate all three current direct `/dev/tty` opens, and add platform-specific tests.

---

## #1394 — Preserve Claude subagent token totals during condensation

### 1. Bug real on current main? **Yes, but only in a narrower case**

The original general loss during ordinary post-`SaveStep` condensation has already been fixed:

- `manual_commit_condensation.go:564-570` restores the checkpoint-scoped value from `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`.
- `manual_commit_condensation.go:1129-1155` documents and implements `withSubagentTokensFrom`.
- Targeted current-main subagent accounting tests pass.

Passing `subagentsDir=""` is now deliberate, not an unexplained leftover:

- Shadow path rationale: `manual_commit_condensation.go:1464-1471`
- Live path rationale: `manual_commit_condensation.go:1513-1517`

There is still a documented gap:

- `manual_commit_condensation.go:1145-1148`: a mid-turn commit before any `SaveStep` has no `CheckpointTokenUsage`, so subagent tokens are omitted.

The PR’s test constructs exactly this no-`SaveStep` scenario.

### 2. PR fix correct and complete? **No**

The directory shape matches today’s centralized `paths.SubagentsDir` convention:

```text
<transcript directory>/<agent session ID>/subagents
```

It is consumed only by agents implementing `SubagentAwareExtractor`, currently principally Claude Code and the compatible Factory implementation.

But the accounting is wrong for repeated checkpoints:

- Subagent extraction returns a **cumulative-since-session-start** snapshot.
- The PR places that cumulative value directly into checkpoint metadata.
- After a prior checkpoint, it must instead subtract `SubagentTokensBaseline`; otherwise later checkpoints re-report earlier subagent usage and aggregate totals double-count it.
- The PR unnecessarily re-reads subagent files on the shadow path, despite the measured cost and the fact those files may already have been cleaned up.
- Its test only checks the first checkpoint, so it misses the double-counting case.

### 3. Recommendation: **Needs rework and rebase**

Limit the fix to the live, pre-`SaveStep` path; use `paths.SubagentsDir`; rescope the cumulative result against `SubagentTokensBaseline`; and test a second checkpoint/window.

Relevant already-landed work a reviewer can cite:

- `a5cf26df89b4a4f76597b216643941b254950e7f` — **fix(checkpoint): carry subagent tokens through to committed checkpoints**
- `80094e5037dc5032bd150955a815e3d85b0d74a8` — follow-up consolidating the correct accounting and documenting the remaining gap

---

## #1408 — Fix rewind of tracked checkpoint deletions

### 1. Bug real on current main? **No—the worktree rewind feature no longer exists**

Your starting point is stale here. Current main has no production `Rewind`, `PreviewRewind`, or `CanRewind`. `manual_commit_rewind.go` now retains only pending-checkpoint listing and logs-only restore behavior.

The old implementation did have the reported bug. I independently ran the PR’s regression scenario:

- Against the parent implementation, preview failed to include `delete-me.txt`.
- Against the PR, the test passed and the tracked file was removed.

So the historical diagnosis was valid, but there is no current command on which it can manifest.

### 2. PR fix correct and complete? **Historically sound, now obsolete**

For the removed implementation:

- Reconciling tracked HEAD paths absent from the checkpoint was the correct behavior.
- Propagating the `Tree.Files().ForEach` error was an improvement. The previous ignored error could allow cancellation to produce an incomplete tracked-file set and then continue restoration.
- Preview and execution were updated consistently.

The test itself would need modernization under current repository standards (`testutil.InitRepo` rather than direct `git.PlainInit`), but the entire tested production path has since been deleted.

### 3. Recommendation: **Close as obsolete/already removed**

Human-citable reference:

- `74e9f831070f19325bb88a7d994c3f3a814cbfe8` — **Remove the restore half of the rewind machinery**

That commit explicitly records that the rewind commands had already disappeared, the restore methods had no reachable production callers, and only logs-only restoration remains. `AGENTS.md:1388` documents the same current architecture.

---

## #1391 — Centralize form accessibility behavior

### 1. Bug real on current main? **No**

Current production form construction is centralized:

- The sole direct non-test `huh.NewForm` call is `cmd/entire/cli/uiform/uiform.go:83`.
- `uiform.New` applies both the shared theme and `ACCESSIBLE` handling.
- CLI-local `NewAccessibleForm` still exists at `cmd/entire/cli/utils.go:24-27` and delegates to `uiform.New`.

The old strategy `isAccessibleMode` helper is gone.

### 2. PR fix correct and complete? **Behavior already landed independently**

The behavior was implemented by:

- `b08f4ce6effaee6119855a368c5ace2b0c574d93` — **Route remaining huh forms through the base16 palette theme**

Unlike the PR, that commit correctly removed the now-unused strategy helper rather than retaining it with `//nolint:unused`.

The PR’s source-level guard test is **not present on main**. Its intent remains worthwhile: prevent future production code from calling `huh.NewForm` outside `uiform`. I would salvage that as a separate small change, preferably following the repository’s existing source-guard patterns.

### 3. Recommendation: **Close as already fixed**

Cite `b08f4ce6effaee6119855a368c5ace2b0c574d93`. Land the guard separately if desired.

### Documentation side finding

The documentation is only **partly** stale:

- `CLAUDE.md:1570-1585` remains valid for code in package `cli`, because `NewAccessibleForm` still exists and delegates correctly.
- `CLAUDE.md:1587-1601` is stale: it instructs strategy code to use the removed `isAccessibleMode` helper and direct `huh.NewForm`.
- `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`, so one edit fixes both.

That section should direct non-`cli` packages, including strategy, to `uiform.New`.
so any suggestion what to do here, did the author act on those PRs after opening, like fixed conflicts or addressed copilot? if not I'd suggest we take over the PRs and get them in the right state?

The contributor did essentially no follow-up work after opening them.

### Activity check

- **#1396:** One commit only. No reviews, comments, follow-up pushes, or visible Copilot feedback. Last meaningful activity was opening day, June 9.
- **#1394:** Force-pushed while preparing the PR, then left one self-review comment explaining their reasoning. No code changes afterward and no external/Copilot review.
- **#1408:** One commit only. No reviews, comments, follow-up pushes, or visible Copilot feedback.
- **#1391:** The branch received a merge from `main` on June 15, authored by Soph, followed by Soph’s request to remove `isAccessibleMode`. The contributor never responded or updated the code afterward.

## Suggested disposition

| PR | Action |
|---|---|
| **#1396** | **Take over and replace/update it.** Real, high-priority Windows bug. Start from current `main`; the old branch is too divergent and needs architectural rework, not conflict resolution. Credit/link the original PR. |
| **#1394** | **Maintainer follow-up for the remaining narrow gap.** Most of the reported bug landed independently in `a5cf26df8`; the existing PR’s accounting is wrong across checkpoint windows. Implement the documented pre-`SaveStep` gap correctly on current main, then close #1394 as superseded. |
| **#1408** | **Close, do not take over.** The affected rewind functionality was removed by `74e9f8310`. |
| **#1391** | **Close, do not take over.** The production behavior landed independently in `b08f4ce6e`. Separately add the source guard and correct the stale strategy accessibility instructions. |

I would not push thousands of current-main commits and major rewrites into the contributor’s old branches. For **#1396** and the remaining **#1394** gap, fresh maintainer branches/PRs are cleaner, with “Supersedes #…” and contributor credit where their work is reused. That also makes review history accurately reflect that the final implementation is materially different.
ok, 1408 and 1391 are closed. I'd also close 1394 then and do a new PR with a fix, would close then when this is in. do the same for 1396, can we do this one after another

5. `/dev/tty` probe, plus its terminal mode → a terminal held in raw mode
   (canonical input off) belongs to a full-screen TUI that spawned us, not to a
   shell we can prompt: TUI git clients (lazygit, gitui, tig) run `git commit`

   must not prompt on. Fails open when the mode can't be read. See

edits.newText:
5. Controlling-terminal probe — `/dev/tty` on Unix, `CONIN$` + `CONOUT$` on
   Windows. On Unix, a terminal held in raw mode (canonical input off) belongs
   to a full-screen TUI that spawned us, not to a shell we can prompt: TUI git
   clients (lazygit, gitui, tig) run `git commit` as a child while owning the
   screen, so the hook inherits a `/dev/tty` it must not prompt on. The mode
   check fails open when it cannot read the mode. See `interactive/tty_*.go`
   and `interactive/rawmode_unix.go` for the platform split and rationale.

edits.oldText:

`interactive.UnderTest()` returns true when `testing.Testing()` or `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY` is set — use it where code needs to skip a real-terminal operation even if `CanPromptInteractively()` returns true (e.g., reading from `/dev/tty` directly inside `askConfirmTTY`).
